Who is behind this work? 
Hi, I’m Evy Olivia Diepenbroek
settings.homeHeroBody: I’m a Designer. always chasing what's next. I'm currently a nominated graphic designer with two degrees in the field and over 4 years of agency experience.
settings.aboutHeroHeading: Hi, I’m Evy Olivia Diepenbroek. Nice to meet you!
settings.aboutHeroLede: I’m a Graphic Designer, always chasing what’s next. I’m driven by new challenges and staying ahead of trends, and I’m currently a nominated graphic designer with two degrees in the field and over 5 years of agency experience.
settings.aboutHeroDetail1: I am a creative with two degrees in Graphic and Communication Design. I began my design journey at Grafisch Lyceum Rotterdam in the Netherlands, where I studied Corporate Design and was selected for the Masterclass as one of the top students in my first year. I then earned a Bachelor’s in Graphic Communication from The University of Northampton in the UK. I concluded my studies with a nomination for The Penguin Book Cover Design Award 2022.
settings.aboutHeroDetail2: I have several years of agency experience as a brand designer, creating and maintaining comprehensive visual identities from logo design and typography to UX design and motion graphics. I’ve collaborated with various creative professionals on projects for major companies like Microsoft and Shell, as well as startups and smaller businesses. Today, I work at a digital agency, where my focus is mainly on digital design.

awards.body: My book design cover was shortlisted for the 2022 Fiction category, Girl, Woman, Other by Bernardine Evaristo with Penguin Random House UK. Everything was incredible. I've learned alot and met some amazing and inspirational people. I'm grateful and honoured to have been selected for this.
awards.title: The Penguin Cover Design Award

awards.body: In this challenge, I won the Motion Design Honorable Mention Prize. The goal was to celebrate authenticity and unique craftsmanship, using the Netherlands as a canvas. Global and RA*W launched the 2024 Digital Out-of-Home challenge, showcasing work on over 2650 digital screens nationwide. The focus was on evoking emotions and inspiring passersby with creativity. I'm honored to be recognized for my contribution.

projects.alt: Spread from the What the F*ck is Blockchain magazine
projects.description: You have probably already heard about its Bitcoin, NFTs or Blockchain. On the news, on social media or just in a conversation. It is everywhere. But what does it all mean? People throw around terms such as blockchain, crypto art, ledger, and NFTs and expect other people to understand what they mean. So, I made a magazine explaining the basics of blockchain in the simplest way possible. This work was also displayed at the NewDesigners exhibition in London.

gallery.heading: It is a lot of information, and after a while reading, that can get too much. That's why after a block of information, you can scan the book and it will come to life.

gallery.body: Throughout the process, I was involved every step of the way. That’s why you’ll see my face multiple times in this magazine ;) All the connections, illustrations, and everything else you see were created by me myself.
gallery.heading: I handled everything from developing the idea and concept to conducting research, writing, collecting content, and designing the visuals.

projects.title: What the F*ck is Blockchain?

projects.description:
Weavr is a B2B growth marketing agency. Its belief is simple: growth only lasts when everything in an organisation is connected, from strategy and people to processes and culture. Weavr helps companies grow from the inside out by bringing insight, structure and direction together in one holistic approach.

I created the full visual identity for Weavr, built around that core idea of connection. The name says it already: weaving separate threads into one strong whole. That thinking runs through the brand, from the logo and visual language to the way every touchpoint fits together.

Beyond the identity, I designed and built the website and a complete set of templates, including PowerPoint and Word templates for daily use and social media templates for consistent communication. The result is a brand that feels as strategic and connected as the work Weavr does for its clients.

Slim verbonden. Gericht op groei.

gallery.body:
Het logo van Weavr draait voornamelijk om de W, een krachtig symbool waarin meerdere betekenissen samenkomen. De W is opgebouwd als een trapje: een opstap naar groei. In de animatie verschijnt de vorm trede voor trede, als metafoor voor de beweging die Weavr in organisaties creëert, gestructureerd, doelgericht, duurzaam en omhoog. 

De trap begint niet helemaal onderaan, maar al een stukje hoger. Dat kleine verschil vertelt iets groots. Bij Weavr begin je niet vanaf nul, maar bouw je verder op wat er al is.

De vorm is strak en eenvoudig, maar heeft zachte, afgeronde hoeken die vriendelijkheid en toegankelijkheid toevoegen. Zo ontstaat een logo dat helder en professioneel is, zonder afstandelijk te worden.

En nog een leuk extra detail: de W kan ook gelezen worden als een omgekeerde M, een knipoog naar oprichter Martijn van Leeuwen.
gallery.heading: Het samen weven van alle draden tot een sterk geheel. Alles met elkaar verbonden.

projects.title: Weavr

projects.alt: Illuminated typography installation in an alley
projects.description: This alley is mainly known as the pissing alley, but also as a scary alley where you don’t want to be in the evening. I have highlighted this with all kinds of colourful typography that also refer to the text that is there. With all kinds of jokes about peeing, it is already a nice place for an Instagram story. But when I looked at my target group I saw that most young people who come here find the most important thing in the evening to show where they have been out on social media. I could use this to make this alley safer as well because no one wants to appear naked or peeing on Instagram. Therefore, by having large luminous letters stuck between the walls I made it a perfect place to take pictures for. Plus it lights up the alley too.
projects.title: My Type Of Place

projects.description:
My dissertation was a big part of my graduation, I chose to make it about the "Narrow Vision Of Design, How new technology is changing the process and psychology of design". a brief introduction to this is this (this can also be read in my desertion):

If you look at the design back in the day, it looked very different than it does now. Nevertheless, one thing that stands out currently is that all design is starting to look more and more alike. The aesthetic of our experiences has changed significantly in the design world. Despite our inability to predict the future, there is still much to be predicted.

We live in a world in which technological advancements are quickly evolving, and we, as graphic designers, are naturally influenced by this. Many new technologies will help graphic designers make better designs and give them more opportunities with extended reality (X.R.), Artificial intelligence (A.I.) and Social Media. However, isn’t this also not the reason for the development of tunnel vision in the creative industry. Fresh ideas and new perspectives are the lifeblood of great work.
projects.title: Dissertation: Narrow Vision of Design

products.alt: Motion Design Styles for Adobe After Effects
products.shortDescription:
A simple design system for After Effects.

Motion Design Styles lets you create, manage, and apply consistent visual styles directly inside After Effects.
Define your Colors, Type, and Variables once, then apply them across your compositions. When you update a style, every layer connected to it updates automatically.
Build your system
Create a central style guide for your project with reusable design tokens.
Stay consistent
Keep typography, colors, corner radii, line weights, and spacing consistent across every composition.
Change once. Update everywhere.
Styles are linked to your layers, so changes to the source style automatically flow through your entire project.
